correctness.rationale: An induction identifies the AND iterate with exact-length predecessor intersections. For t=E-k and 1<=k<=a, all path-length differences exceed c-a, where the semigroup <a,a+1> omits only c-1. Consequently missing predecessors must have alpha+beta=2a+1-k. The two-to-one distance multiplicities yield (2k-1) singleton-zero and (k-1) doubleton-zero survivors. Monotone absorbing zero dynamics gives three states in every late shell and one at E; all other states are zero by E. Complete independent direct-state checks a=2,...,7 (21,840 states) and predecessor-walk checks a=2,...,40 passed from packaged code.

value.rationale: The graph family is a canonical two-feedback-loop Boolean network, and its full terminal window of length a is the natural scale set by the shorter loop. The exact sharp-height count alone is classical and too coarse; a complete terminal first-entry and Hamming-zero-weight census with constant three-state shell sizes is a substantial new quantitative boundary statement. It isolates an interpretable survival mechanism (one zero or a paired zero at matched hub distance), with plausible use in late-extinction probabilities and robustness analysis. The theorem does not depend on arbitrary finite parameter selection or an artificially chosen invariant.
